key_insight: Quantum Hamiltonian embeddings encode a classical training dataset into a parameterized Hamiltonian whose approximate ground state defines a classifier.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports classical or quantum inference from the learned state, offering flexibility for hybrid learning workflows.
method: Encode labeled training data into a single effective Hamiltonian.
Optimize Hamiltonian parameters using efficient gradient-estimation methods.
Approximate the ground state with a quantum algorithm to obtain the classification rule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports favorable generalization guarantees, conditional hardness results for efficient classical algorithms, and a demonstration on IBM Heron processors using a standard benchmark dataset.
watch_item: Practical performance depends on ground-state approximation and state-representation costs; the abstract does not establish an empirical advantage over classical baselines.
paper_title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
